critical_findings.finding: XSS/content injection can ship in the static HTML if Markdown raw HTML is allowed or if templates fail to escape user-controlled strings (titles, tags, link text). This can execute in readers’ browsers, especially when notes are shared publicly.

closure.closure_target: M5 (DL20) + security regression tests before Review/Freeze.
closure.required_actions: Default: disable raw HTML in Markdown rendering or sanitize it; enforce strict template escaping for all user-controlled fields; add test fixtures containing known XSS payloads in Markdown, titles, and tags; document an explicit 'unsafe allow-html' mode behind a flag with warnings.

closure.closure_target: Before implementing M4 search and before claiming R22 performance; add stress tests + instrumentation in Validate.
closure.required_actions: Resolve Q3 scale; add progress logging + per-stage timing/memory metrics; enforce limits (max file size / max notes) with actionable errors; prefer streaming/tokenization where feasible; add stress fixtures at target bounds and verify build completes without OOM/hang.

closure.closure_target: M1 (DL2/DL6) + add cross-platform test matrix before M3 link/backlink work.
closure.required_actions: Normalize canonical IDs using source-relative paths with consistent separators (DEC2); define supported encodings and behavior for invalid bytes (skip with report vs fail); add OS-specific path fixtures (case collisions, Unicode, spaces) and ensure deterministic mapping across platforms.

critical_findings.finding: A trusted user, unaware of the public-facing nature of static hosting, could configure the tool to build from a directory containing private or sensitive notes. Since access control is a non-goal, the generated site, when deployed, would inadvertently expose this sensitive information publicly, representing a catastrophic data leakage failure.

closure.closure_target: Confirm explicit user acceptance of the data exposure risk. Implement the planned README disclaimer (DL21) and add a high-visibility warning message during the build process.

critical_findings.finding: The chosen in-memory graph architecture (O1) creates a failure mode where the build process crashes due to out-of-memory errors or becomes unusably slow when processing a large corpus of notes, preventing users with large note collections from using the tool.

closure.closure_target: Establish and test against defined performance budgets and scale targets (e.g., for 1,000 and 5,000 notes). Implement stress tests in CI to monitor memory/CPU usage and document known limitations, per the mitigation plan for K4.

critical_findings.finding: If a user's Markdown notes contain crafted malicious content (e.g., <script> tags), and the system renders this into the final HTML without proper sanitization, deploying the site creates a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability for any reader of the generated site.

closure.closure_target: Implement and enable HTML sanitization by default for all content rendered from Markdown. Ensure all template variables are contextually escaped, per the mitigation plan in M5/DL20.

critical_findings.finding: The system fails to correctly build the site's primary navigation features (backlinks and tag indexes) due to ambiguity in user conventions (e.g., wiki-links vs. relative links, YAML vs. inline tags), leading to a disconnected note graph and undermining core product goals.

closure.closure_target: Finalize decisions on blocking questions Q1 and Q2. Implement configurable parsers for links and tags with explicit, non-ambiguous settings, and default to the most restrictive standard. This addresses risks K2 & K3.

critical_findings.finding: At scale, the client-side search index may become too large, leading to long page load times and an unresponsive search UI. This would degrade the user experience for a core feature to the point of being unusable.

closure.closure_target: Evaluate and select a client-side search library proven to meet performance targets (R22) at the anticipated scale. Implement performance tests for index size and query latency as part of M4 exit criteria.

critical_findings.finding: The build tool fails or produces incorrect links/assets when run on a different operating system (e.g., Windows vs. Linux) than it was developed on, due to unhandled differences in path separators or file system case-sensitivity.

closure.closure_target: Use OS-agnostic libraries for all path manipulation. Establish a cross-platform CI test matrix (Windows, macOS, Linux) that runs core acceptance tests to prevent regressions, addressing risk K11.
